findings.documented: POST /auth/login returns token with expires_in: 86400 (24 hours); no token refresh flow is supported.
findings.actual: Tokens expire in 900 seconds (15 minutes). Response key is access_token and provides a refresh_url at /auth/refresh.
findings.how_found: Authenticated against POST /auth/login and inspected the response payload keys and expires_in header.
findings.impact: Frontend sessions expire in 15 minutes unless refreshed via /auth/refresh or renewed via login.

findings.documented: POST /auth/logout invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Tokens are stateless JWTs. Server returns {'ok': true, 'note': 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side'} and the token continues to be accepted on subsequent requests.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout with active bearer token and then successfully made authenticated calls with the same token.
findings.impact: Logout must be fully enforced on the client side by purging local storage and cookies.

findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as a query parameter (e.g., ?api_key=IVY26-...).
findings.actual: Query parameter api_key is rejected with HTTP 401: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'.
findings.how_found: Sent requests with ?api_key=... and received HTTP 401 error message specifying the X-API-Key requirement.
findings.impact: All API requests from frontend and scripts must transmit the key via X-API-Key HTTP header.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page (default 1) and limit (maximum 200), returning { total, page, page_size, results }.
findings.actual: The page parameter is quietly ignored; pagination uses 0-indexed offset. Maximum limit is capped at 50. Response contains { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results }.
findings.how_found: Tested varying page and limit parameters, verifying returned results and metadata.
findings.impact: Pagination must increment offset by page size (at most 50) and continue until has_more is False.

findings.documented: total in collection response represents the exact number of retrievable records.
findings.actual: The total field reports 4659, but paging past offset 4659 until has_more is False retrieves 5100 valid, distinct listings.
findings.how_found: Paged past reported total 4659 until has_more became False at offset 5100.
findings.impact: Relying on total causes truncation of 441 valid listing records.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Returns both active listings (is_live: true, 4017 records) and inactive/withdrawn listings (is_live: false, 1083 records).
findings.how_found: Inspected is_live boolean property across all 5100 retrievable listing records.
findings.impact: Client-side filtering is mandatory to prevent showing expired or inactive listings to buyers.

findings.documented: Property listings satisfy standard physical and geographic constraints (carpet <= super_built, floor <= total_floors, positive price, Mumbai bounds).
findings.actual: Contains 44 corrupt records: 11 with carpet > super_built, 11 with floor > total_floors, 11 with negative price, and 11 with latitude and longitude swapped.
findings.how_found: Ran systematic validation checks across all physical, structural, and geographic fields.
findings.impact: Corrupt listings must be sanitized or excluded from average metrics and user-facing feeds.

findings.documented: posted_by_contact is the seller's verified contact number corresponding to an individual real property.
findings.actual: 10 telemarketing phone numbers flood the listings with 19 to 38 listings each (313 total fake/lead-gen listings) across disparate localities and property types.
findings.how_found: Performed frequency distribution analysis on posted_by_contact phone numbers.
findings.impact: Enquiry-bait listings skew price-per-sqft analytics and clutter user search feeds.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 42 listings describe 21 duplicate physical properties posted simultaneously across multiple aggregator platforms (zerobroker, magichomes, dwelling) with identical floor, carpet area, BHK, and building.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by (apartment_name, locality, bedroom, floor, carpet_area) and inspected duplicate pairs.
findings.impact: De-duplication is necessary to present clean, unique property options to end users.

findings.documented: Accepts project_id query parameter to filter listings belonging to a specific builder project.
findings.actual: The project_id query parameter is quietly ignored by GET /v1/listings, returning the unfiltered listing collection.
findings.how_found: Sent requests with ?project_id=P50001 and observed unfiltered response count and mismatched project IDs.
findings.impact: Filtering listings by project must be executed on the client side.

findings.documented: Accepts order='desc' alongside sort_by parameter to sort results in descending order.
findings.actual: The order parameter is ignored; queries with sort_by=price&order=desc return records in ascending order identical to order=asc.
findings.how_found: Compared result sequences of sort_by=price with order=asc and order=desc.
findings.impact: Descending sorting must be applied client-side after retrieving records.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in integer Indian rupees everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: price_max is expressed in Crores (e.g. 12.44 representing ₹12.44 Cr), and several projects have price_min in Lakhs (e.g. 99.3 Lakhs) while price_max is in Crores (4.24 Cr), causing price_min > price_max.
findings.how_found: Audited price ranges in /v1/projects and identified mixed units across price_min and price_max.
findings.impact: UI must normalize price units and detect inverted price ranges.

findings.documented: total_listings in /v1/projects always agrees with the number of available listings with matching project_id.
findings.actual: total_listings disagrees with actual retrievable listings referencing project_id for 446 of the 590 projects.
findings.how_found: Cross-referenced total_listings from /v1/projects with the count of listings referencing each project_id in /v1/listings.
findings.impact: Frontend project cards should display actual verified listing counts instead of static total_listings.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing object.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns HTTP 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is pluralized: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request to /v1/listing/{listing_id} with valid ID and received 404.
findings.impact: All property detail routing must call /v1/listings/{id}.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to 10 comparable listings.
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 404 Not Found for all listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings/{id}/similar for multiple verified listing IDs and received 404.
findings.impact: Similar listings recommendation strip must be computed client-side by matching locality, BHK, and price band.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.how_found: Attempted to GET /v1/analytics/summary and received 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Insights and analytics dashboards must calculate market metrics directly from listings and rentals data.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage user saved listings.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found for GET, POST, and DELETE.
findings.how_found: Tested GET, POST, and DELETE on /v1/favourites with valid tokens and received 404.
findings.impact: Saved listings must be persisted client-side per user (e.g. localStorage / IndexedDB).

findings.documented: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: GET /health returns server_time with an explicit Indian Standard Time offset (+05:30) instead of UTC with Z suffix.
findings.how_found: Inspected JSON response from unauthenticated GET /health endpoint.
findings.impact: Client timestamp parsers must support explicit timezone offsets alongside UTC Z timestamps.
